positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description: I implemented an indexing system for and added S3 partial object read support to Bloomberg Ticker Plant's compressed historical market datastore, and prototyped an integration of this compressed store into Ticker Plant's primary timeseries database.  These added features improved the read performance of the historical datastore by up to 100× for both local and networked archives and introduced a path forward for offloading market data into a compressed format with minimal performance degradation.  I also served as the inaugural Scrum Master for my team, moderating discussions and helping to direct the team's development trajectory.

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description:
I designed and implemented a project to concurrently compute historic economic index values using Adobe Spark running under Python.  As a portion of this program, I also designed and implemented an API for defining custom calculations callable via JSON requests, and wrote a static analyzer for Python in order to determine the relationships between these calculations and store them in a SQLite-alike database.  The final outcome of this project was a 3–10× performance improvement for billion-data-point operations over the previous index computation system.

As an adjacent project, I also designed and implemented a parser and serializer for an extended SQL dialect to be used for querying historical index data.  Designed for a team adjacent to my own, this project was used by multiple teams in the Bloomberg Index department.

volunteerExperiences.description: I managed a volunteer program that instructs members of the North Texas community in all levels of figure skating. In addition to administering the program, I also wrote software for the City, designed and wrote publications for City events, and taught nine figure skating classes weekly.

I wrote the website and financial tracking system for a week-long benefit event that raised over $10,000 for Austin Street Center, a local homeless shelter. I also held an active leadership position in the organization of this event.

projects.title: Hudson
projects.description: A multi-paradigm programming language inspired by OCaml, Haskell, and Ada designed with the goal of being usable on machines from 1980 onward.  The language, written in C with Assembly platform bridges, will include modern language features such as extended Hindley-Milner type inference and limited algebraic effects.  The language's parser is implemented using a parser combinator library that I wrote and have extracted from the Hudson core for use in other projects.

projects.title: el-Emeñir
projects.description: A historical constructed language that aims to predict how the ancient Sumerian language would have changed if it survived into the modern era.  This project involves 2000 years of historical linguistic research, as well as linguistic knowledge of Sumerian, Akkadian, Elamite, Aramaic, medieval Syriac, classical Arabic, and modern Iraqi Arabic.  I am currently preparing public documentation of the language for the constructed languages community.

In addition to administering the program, I also wrote software for the City, designed and wrote publications for City events, and taught nine figure skating classes weekly.

organizations.name: St. Mark's Classics Club
organizations.description: I led an organization that aims to promote interest in the Classics among the students of the St. Mark's School of Texas.  Through close collaboration with the St. Mark's Classics Department, we met great success at local and state Latin competitions; in addition, I wrote extensive documentation of the grammar and syntax of the classical Latin language.  Finally, I instructed two Latin students of my own, with both progressing through over a year of curriculum in under two months.
